bib.venue: O'Reilly, Python for Data Analysis 2nd ed., ch. 5, pp. 123-165

question: What are pandas' two core data structures, Series and DataFrame, and the essential operations (reindexing, selection, alignment, sorting, reductions) on them?

results.claim: Label-based slicing includes the endpoint, unlike Python slicing.
results.setup: Series obj with index a,b,c,d; obj['b':'c'] returns b and c
results.quote: Slicing with labels behaves differently than normal Python slicing in that the end‐ point is inclusive:
results.note: Quote uses a soft hyphen line break in the PDF; if the check fails use the table-free claim form.

results.claim: Adding two Series with partly different labels gives the union of labels, with NaN where labels do not overlap (an outer join on the index).
results.setup: s1 (index a,c,d,e) + s2 (index a,c,e,f,g): a 5.2, c 1.1, e 0.0, d/f/g NaN
results.quote: The internal data alignment introduces missing values in the label locations that don’t overlap.

results.claim: add with fill_value=0 treats a label missing from one frame as 0 instead of NaN.
results.setup: df1 (3x4) and df2 (4x5, with df2.loc[1,'b']=NaN); df1.add(df2, fill_value=0) gives row 3 equal to df2 row 3 (15.0 16.0 17.0 18.0 19.0)

results.claim: rank breaks ties by average rank by default; method='first' ranks by order of appearance.
results.setup: obj = Series([7,-5,7,4,2,0,4]); obj.rank() gives 6.5 to the two 7s; method='first' gives 6 and 7
results.quote: Here, instead of using the average rank 6.5 for the entries 0 and 2, they instead have been set to 6 and 7 because label 0 precedes label 2 in the data.

limits: Written for pandas of about 0.20 (2017) and Python 3.6; later pandas removed or changed much of it.

Dated in pandas 2/3: ix (the chapter itself calls it deprecated) and get_value/set_value are removed; DataFrame.mad removed; Int64Index removed (plain Index with int64 dtype); pd.value_counts top-level and data.apply(pd.value_counts) deprecated in 2.x, use Series.value_counts; applymap renamed DataFrame.map; Index.is_monotonic removed (use is_monotonic_increasing); the level argument on reductions removed (use groupby); 'match' in Table 5-9 does not exist as a method; Series obj[1] / obj[[1,3]] positional fallback on a non-integer index is deprecated and removed in pandas 3, use iloc.

pandas 3 adds Copy-on-Write as the only behaviour: the chapter's claim that a column from df[col] is a view whose in-place changes show up in the DataFrame no longer holds. Also string columns default to a dedicated str dtype instead of object, so the object dtype outputs shown (e.g. frame2['state'], values arrays) differ. inplace=True is discouraged. Verify these against current release notes; they are from knowledge, not from the chapter.
pandas_datareader get_data_yahoo example no longer works; the chapter itself warns Yahoo may disappear.
Dict-constructed DataFrame columns are shown sorted (pop, state, year); since Python 3.7 and pandas 0.23 insertion order is kept.
No performance, memory or internals coverage; the chapter says DataFrame internals are out of scope.
practices: Use loc for label-based and iloc for integer-based selection rather than ix or bare [] on integer indexes (p. 144-145).
With an integer axis index, [] selection is always label-oriented, so use loc or iloc for precise handling (p. 145).
Use loc as a succinct replacement for reindex; many users use it exclusively (p. 138).
Be careful with inplace=True because it destroys dropped data (p. 140).
Use the flexible arithmetic methods (add, sub, etc.) with fill_value or axis='index' to control alignment and broadcasting direction (p. 148-151).
Copy a column explicitly with Series.copy if you do not want in-place changes to reach the DataFrame (p. 132).
Avoid duplicate index labels where possible because selection return type varies between Series and scalar (p. 157).

terms.definition: A one-dimensional array-like object containing a sequence of values (of similar types to NumPy types) and an associated array of data labels, called its index.
A rectangular table of data and contains an ordered collection of columns, each of which can be a different value type; it can be thought of as a dict of Series all sharing the same index.
Index objects hold the axis labels and other metadata (like the axis name or names); they are immutable and can contain duplicates.
Create a new object with the data conformed to a new index.
Arithmetic between objects with different indexes yields the union of the index pairs, like an automatic outer join on the index labels.
Subtracting a row from a 2D array performs the subtraction once for each row.
Methods that extract a single value (like the sum or mean) from a Series or a Series of values from the rows or columns of a DataFrame.

lineage.note: pandas adopts NumPy's array-based idioms; Series and DataFrame ops build on ndarray and ufuncs.
